He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]] and was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[2023 NBA draft]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. ==Early life and high school career== Whitmore attended [[Archbishop Spalding High School]] in [[Severn, Maryland]]. As a senior, he was the ''[[Capital Gazette]]'' boys basketball player of the year.{{cite web|url=https://www.capitalgazette.com/sports/high-school/ac-cs-cam-whitmore-anne-arundel-2022-boys-basketball-all-county-20220409-7iydoeszgjdjdjnmg2mynsxx3m-story.html |title=Archbishop Spalding's Cam Whitmore caps decorated career as 2021–22 Capital Gazette boys basketball Player of Year – Capital Gazette |publisher=Capitalgazette.com |date= |accessdate=July 24, 2022}} He was selected to play in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2022/01/25/spalding-boys-basketball-star-cam-whitmore-selected-to-play-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game/ |title=Spalding boys basketball star Cam Whitmore selected to play in McDonald's All American game – Baltimore Sun |publisher=Baltimoresun.com |date= |access-date=July 24, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2022/03/30/archbishop-spaldings-cam-whitmore-has-19-points-including-monstrous-dunk-in-east-win-in-mcdonalds-basketball-game/ |title=Archbishop Spalding's Cam Whitmore has 19 points, including monstrous dunk, in East win in McDonald's basketball game – Baltimore Sun |publisher=Baltimoresun.com |date= |access-date=July 24, 2022}} He played in the [[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]], where he was named MVP.{{cite web|last=Aiello |first=Thomas |url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/cam-whitmore-dominates-at-fiba-u18-for-team-usa/ |title=Cam Whitmore Dominates for Team USA at FIBA U18 | SLAM |publisher=Slamonline.com |date=June 13, 2022 |accessdate=July 24, 2022}} ===Recruiting=== Whitmore was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. On October 7, 2021, he to playing college basketball for [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] over offers from [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/10/07/cam-whitmore-spaldings-five-star-basketball-prospect-commits-villanova/ |title=Cam Whitmore, Spalding's five-star basketball prospect, commits to Villanova |date=October 8, 2021 |author1=Kyle Melnick |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |place=Washington, D.C. |issn=0190-8286 |oclc=1330888409}}{{cite web | url=https://www.mdjonline.com/fieldlevel/five-star-f-cam-whitmore-commits-to-villanova/article_f07d4dea-8643-5bc6-a2e2-223a46dfd209.html | title=Five-star F Cam Whitmore commits to Villanova }}{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32356213/top-40-recruit-cameron-whitmore-verbally-commits-villanova-wildcats | title=Top-40 recruit Whitmore commits to Villanova | date=October 7, 2021 }} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2022}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Cam Whitmore | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Odenton, Maryland|Odenton, MD]] | highschool = [[Archbishop Spalding High School|Archbishop Spalding]] (MD) | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 220 | 40 = | commitdate = October 7, 2021 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | On3 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 90 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2022 | rivals ref title = Villanova 2022 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2022 Villanova Wildcats Recruiting Class | rivals school = villanova | scout s = | espn schoolid = 222 | rivals overall = 10 | 247 overall = 11 | On3 overall = 7 | espn overall = 22 | accessdate = November 20, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== After missing seven games with a thumb injury, Whitmore made his collegiate debut versus Oklahoma. In his first season with Villanova, Whitmore averaged 12.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 0.7 assists per game. At the conclusion of his freshman year, Whitmore was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year]]. He later declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], becoming Villanova's first true one-and-done since [[Tim Thomas (basketball)|Tim Thomas]] in 1997.{{cite web |last1=Rapay |first1=Eugene |title=Villanova’s Cam Whitmore declares for 2023 NBA Draft |url=https://www.vuhoops.com/villanova-basketball/2023/4/12/23679878/villanova-wildcats-cam-whitmore-declares-for-2023-nba-draft Draft|last=Siegel|first=Brett|website=ClutchPoints|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 24, 2023}} On October 26, 2023, he made his NBA debut in a 116–86 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]]{{Cite web |title=Rockets 86–116 Magic (Oct 25, 2023) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401584694 |access-date=October 26, 2023 |website=ESPN |language=en}} and made his first NBA start on January 21, 2024, in a home loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |date=January 21, 2024 |title=Rockets' Cam Whitmore: Will make first career start |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-cam-whitmore-will-make-first-career-start/ |access-date=January 22, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Cam Whitmore {{!}} Houston Rockets |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1641715/cam-whitmore/ |access-date=January 22, 2024 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} On January 26, 2024, Whitmore recorded his first career double-double and his then-career high, recording 24 points, 11 rebounds and 2 assists on 50% shooting (44% from three) in a 138–104 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |title=Cam Whitmore {{!}} Houston Rockets |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1641715/cam-whitmore/ |access-date=January 27, 2024 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Most Double Doubles By Rookies In The NBA This Season |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/most-double-doubles-by-rookies-in-the-nba-this-season |access-date=January 27, 2024 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Jalen Green scores 36 points to help Rockets rout Hornets 138–104 |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/jalen-green-scores-36-points-rockets-rout-hornets-106727559 |access-date=January 27, 2024 |website=ABC News |language=en}} Whitmore led the NBA in points per touch and averaged 23.7 points per 36 minutes in his rookie season.{{cite news |last1=Shapiro |first1=Michael |title=‘Can't get me nowhere’: Rockets star bristles at lack of minutes |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/cam-whitmore-postgame-video-mavericks-20011734.php |access-date=May 1, 2025 |work=Chron |date=January 2, 2025 |language=en}} In his second season, Whitmore's playing time decreased with [[Tari Eason]] returning from injury. He had several assignments with Rio Grande Valley.{{cite news |last1=Lerner |first1=Danielle |title=Cam Whitmore wants to play his way back into the Rockets rotation. 'I'm gonna keep grinding' |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/rockets/article/cam-whitmore-minutes-stats-19992681.php |access-date=May 1, 2025 |work=Houston Chronicle |date=December 20, 2024}} On April 11, 2025, Whitmore scored a career-high 34 points in a 140–109 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite news |title=Lakers 140-109 Rockets (Apr 11, 2025) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705751 |access-date=April 12, 2025 |work=ESPN |date=April 11, 2025 |language=en}} === Washington Wizards (2025–2026) === On July 5, 2025, the [[Washington Wizards]] acquired Whitmore in a three-team trade also involving the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=July 5, 2025 |title=Rockets trade Whitmore to Wizards for 2 second-round picks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45678556/sources-rockets-trade-whitmore-wizards-two-seconds |access-date=July 5, 2025 |publisher=ESPN}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-complete-three-team-trade-2|title=Wizards Complete Three-Team Trade |publisher=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2025|access-date=July 7, 2025}} The trade also involved another former [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcat]], as [[Saddiq Bey]] was traded from the Wizards to the Pelicans.{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Pelicans complete three-team trade with Washington Wizards and Houston Rockets {{!}} New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://pelicans.com/news/jordan-poole-saddiq-bey-trade-washington-wizards-nba-free-agency-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-july-6-2025 |access-date=2025-10-31 |website=pelicans.com |language=en}} On October 22, 2025, Whitmore made his Wizards debut. He scored 14 points and secured five rebounds in 19 minutes, coming off the bench for the Wizards. The Wizards lost 133-120 against the [[2025–26 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whitmca01/gamelog/2026|title=Cam Whitmore 2025-26 Game Log |publisher=basketball-reference.com|date=October 23, 2025|access-date=October 31, 2025}} He made 21 appearances for Washington during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 9.2 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 0.7 assists. On December 23, Whitmore was diagnosed with upper-extremity [[deep vein thrombosis]] in his right shoulder.{{Cite web|title=Wizards F Cam Whitmore diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47400614/wizards-whitmore-diagnosed-deep-vein-thrombosis|access-date=February 1, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On January 15, 2026, Whitmore was ruled out for the remainder of the season as a result of the diagnosis.{{Cite web|title=Wizards' Cam Whitmore out for remainder of season with deep-vein thrombosis|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/wizards-cam-whitmore-out-for-season-with-deep-vein-thrombosis/|access-date=February 1, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On August 21, 2026, Whitmore was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a five-team trade, but he was waived shortly after.{{Cite web |title=Cavaliers Acquire Peyton Watson |url=https://cavs.com/news/releases-peyton-watson-260821 |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=cavs.com |language=en}} ==Player profile== Standing at 6-foot-6 and 235 pounds, Whitmore plays at the small forward position. At the 2023 NBA Combine, Whitmore finished third in max vertical leap (40.5 inches). Scouts viewed Whitmore as a versatile wing with tremendous upside and athleticism. Offensively, he can effectively use a range of dribble moves to score in transition against similarly sized defenders.{{Cite web |title=Cam Whitmore |url=https://www.nbadraft.net/players/cam-whitmore/ |access-date=September 22, 2023 |website=NBADraft.net |language=en-US}} Coming into the league, commentators noted his half-court scoring, vision, and IQ as weaknesses.
